Fixing startup, sound and save problems

Most startup failures print their reason to a terminal. Start the game from a terminal first, then use the matching section below.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 5 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Read the startup message
  2. Worlds that will not load
  3. Saving and losing progress
  4. Graphics driver problems
  5. Sound and music
  6. How this was checked

Read the startup message

When the game cannot start, it closes and prints the reason to the terminal. Menu and desktop launches show no error window, so start Voxelgame from a terminal to read the message.

  • voxelgame could not start: ... means a bad option was given. The game exits with code 2.
  • voxelgame failed: ... means any other startup failure. The game exits with code 1.

Messages you may see:

  • no Vulkan-compatible graphics adapter found: the graphics driver is missing. See Graphics driver problems below.
  • GPU ran out of memory during startup: lower Settings > General > Horizon distance, then try again.
  • Nearby terrain took too long to prepare; please try again: shown on the main menu. Try again, or lower Settings > General > Horizon distance.
  • audio disabled: playback command unavailable: sound players are missing. See Sound and music below.

Setup failures are written to an installer log. See Install, update and find your worlds.

Tip. Problems with other worlds appear on the main menu instead of closing the game.

Worlds that will not load

The game never overwrites a world file it cannot read. The file stays as it is, so you can move it or try again later.

A world from the Worlds list fails

The main menu shows world could not be loaded: ... and you stay where you were. Pick another world or fix the file, then try again.

The starting world fails

The game opens the starting world, `worlds/debug/debug.vxw`, or the file named by `VOXELGAME_SAVE_PATH` when you start it. If that file cannot be read, the game closes before the main menu and prints the reason to the terminal.

  1. Close the game.
  2. Move the damaged `.vxw` file to a backup folder. Do not delete it.
  3. Start the game again. A new starting world is created when the file is missing.
Careful. Moving the file aside means the game starts with a new starting world. Keep the old file if you may want its contents back. Find the data folder with Install, update and find your worlds.

Saving and losing progress

Press F6 in a world to save now. The game also saves when you choose Main menu or Save & quit in the Esc menu, press Ctrl+Q, close the window, or load or create another world. Autosave runs every 30 seconds when the world has changed.

Tip. Autosave runs after changes such as building, mining, home storage, journal edits or boats. Walking around and most crafting wait for the next F6 or quit, so press F6 after a long crafting session.

If saving fails while you quit, the game stays open. Fix the cause, such as a full disk, and save again.

Good to know. There is no crash recovery. A crash loses changes made since the last save. The previous save file is kept intact.

Graphics driver problems

Voxelgame needs a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux it runs in an X11 or XWayland session. It has no native Wayland window.

  • Debian and Fedora: the installer adds Mesa Vulkan drivers.
  • Arch: install vulkan-intel or vulkan-radeon, or your NVIDIA driver.
  • macOS: a Metal-capable GPU is required.

The game picks your high-performance GPU first. If that fails, it falls back to a software renderer such as llvmpipe. The fallback is useful for diagnosis but too slow for normal play.

To reduce GPU load, set Settings > General > Horizon distance lower, turn off Settings > Debug > Distant terrain, or set Settings > General > Shader to None.

Careful. Windows graphics have not been validated on a real Windows PC yet.

Sound and music

Sound effects need a player program: aplay from alsa-utils on Linux, or ffplay on Windows and macOS. The installers set these up. Without a player the game runs silently.

Music also needs ffmpeg to decode the songs. Song files may be mp3, ogg, wav or flac.

  • If ffmpeg is missing, Music turns itself off and the status line shows Music unavailable: ....
  • After you install ffmpeg, open Settings > Audio and switch Music back on.

How this guide was checked

Error text, file paths, keys and save rules come from the game and installer source at the audited commit. Each ledger entry lists its source lines.
